Still, the ancient trunks, boughs, and roots of these skyscraper trees knit together to form a traversable environment. In its quiet moments, it seems almost peaceful. (This, of course, is a lie.)

496.title: Sights
496.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › I – The Magician: The Spires › Sights
496.body: A desiccated forest of colossal, dead trees. Everything is eerie. The shadows of the bare branches grasp out towards you like skeletal fingers.

497.title: Sounds
497.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › I – The Magician: The Spires › Sounds
497.body: A constant buzzing from the ubiquitous copper-colored locusts. It sounds like an unplugged mic.

498.title: Smell and taste
498.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › I – The Magician: The Spires › Smell and taste
498.body: The smell of a rotting pumpkin left out well into January. Vegetative humus.

499.title: Lighting
499.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › I – The Magician: The Spires › Lighting
499.body: In the rot of the wood, glowing mushrooms shed a weird half-light. This counts as dim light, equivalent to a moonlit night.

500.title: Structures
500.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › I – The Magician: The Spires › Structures
500.body: Like an Ewok village, wooden bridges connect the islands of trees that hang in the midst of a great emptiness.

501.title: Common monsters
501.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › I – The Magician: The Spires › Common monsters
501.body: Forest Imps, Mushroom Men, Cockatrice, Dire Bats, Dire Wolves, Sword Spiders, Undead Bears, Flower Fairies, Dryads, Lions

502.title: Dungeon lord
502.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › I – The Magician: The Spires › Dungeon lord

503.title: II – The High Priestess: The Boundless Moat
503.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › II – The High Priestess: The Boundless Moat
503.body: Souls aren’t the only things that sink into the Underworld—ships do as well. This level is an underground ocean choked with the wreckage of a thousand, thousand ships. The limitless depths glow a ghastly neon color, casting bizarre shadows up onto the islands of sunken ships. The wreckage islands are a home to pirates, thieves, and worse.

504.title: Sights
504.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › II – The High Priestess: The Boundless Moat › Sights
504.body: Glowing blue waters, like an emptied glowstick. A floating dungeon, bobbing like a cork upon the waves.

505.title: Sounds
505.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › II – The High Priestess: The Boundless Moat › Sounds
505.body: The constant push and pull of the waves sounds like the snoring of a giant; like an hourglass being constantly turned. Psssssh. Thrsssssh.

506.title: Smell and taste
506.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › II – The High Priestess: The Boundless Moat › Smell and taste
506.body: The air tastes and smells of salt. The air is humid. Your armor requires constant oiling or it will rust.

507.title: Lighting
507.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › II – The High Priestess: The Boundless Moat › Lighting
507.body: The waves shine with glowing blue bioluminescent waters; this provides dim light.

508.title: Structures
508.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › II – The High Priestess: The Boundless Moat › Structures
508.body: Rafts of bobbing flotsam and jetsam stretch across the underground ocean. Chambers of wreckage, hallways made of gangplanks, and a few solid reefs tying everything together.

509.title: Common monsters
509.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › II – The High Priestess: The Boundless Moat › Common monsters
509.body: Brine Imps, Sirens, Vodyanoy, Kraken, Daggerfish, Dire Man o’ Wars, Dire Eels, Kelpies, Leviathans

510.title: Dungeon lord
510.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › II – The High Priestess: The Boundless Moat › Dungeon lord

511.title: III – The Empress: The Castle of Crossed Destinies
511.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › III – The Empress: The Castle of Crossed Destinies
511.body: The Castle of Crossed Destinies was the seat of power for the Triarchy. The decadence that this castle once knew has faded and grown tarnished as it has fallen to the influences of the Underworld. Incredible works of art and unknowable traps sit side by side in these ancient halls. The castle is tended by a caste of degenerate servants called the Lavritic who are descended from the original inhabitants. They trim the wicks of candles, throw dead bodies out of windows, and reset the traps. They are bound by powerful geas to never interfere, harm, or help outsiders. At best, they prostrate themselves and tremble.

512.title: Sights
512.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › III – The Empress: The Castle of Crossed Destinies › Sights
512.body: Grand rooms filled with magnificent works of baroque art. Utterly old and utterly beautiful.

513.title: Sounds
513.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › III – The Empress: The Castle of Crossed Destinies › Sounds
513.body: Eerily silent except for your own footsteps .

514.title: Smell and taste
514.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › III – The Empress: The Castle of Crossed Destinies › Smell and taste
514.body: Everything smells old, dusty, and moldy .

515.title: Lighting
515.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › III – The Empress: The Castle of Crossed Destinies › Lighting
515.body: Candles light most rooms and hallways. They are regularly tended by the Lavritic.

516.title: Structures
516.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › III – The Empress: The Castle of Crossed Destinies › Structures
516.body: Hallways and chambers made of cold, fitted stones. Wooden doors set with lever door knobs.

517.title: Common monsters
517.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › III – The Empress: The Castle of Crossed Destinies › Common monsters
517.body: Painted Imps, Dire Rats, Living Armor, Living Paintings, Mimics (Chests, Treasure, Ladders), Gargoyles, the First Knights

518.title: Dungeon lord
518.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › III – The Empress: The Castle of Crossed Destinies › Dungeon lord

519.title: IV – The Emperor: The Inverted Castle
519.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IV – The Emperor: The Inverted Castle
519.body: Dripping down like a stalactite, the Inverted Castle hangs in the midst of a great cavern. The draconic children of His Majesty the Worm are entombed here, and their reality-warping influence seeps out of their prison-tombs. Each room of the Inverted Castle seems to be decorated by someone who has only heard about humans through unreliable ancient historians and seen pictures of their lives through crude art. The rooms appear to be set to some purpose, but there’s little logic to the layout, decoration, or inventory. Disparate concepts are juxtaposed. Certain rooms are laid out nonsensically, e.g., an entire wing is entirely upside down.

520.title: Sights
520.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IV – The Emperor: The Inverted Castle › Sights
520.body: Escher-esque hallways tangled around a central Rubik’s Cube of a room. Disproportionate furniture hangs from the walls and the ceiling. An enshrined dragon is mummified in paper ofuda.

521.title: Sounds
521.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IV – The Emperor: The Inverted Castle › Sounds
521.body: The hanging towers ring their bells hourly. Their tintinnabulations reverberate through the entire structure.

522.title: Smell and taste
522.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IV – The Emperor: The Inverted Castle › Smell and taste
522.body: The air is dry and warm, with a faint tang of iron.

523.title: Lighting
523.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IV – The Emperor: The Inverted Castle › Lighting

524.title: Structures
524.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IV – The Emperor: The Inverted Castle › Structures
524.body: Hallways and chambers made of cold, fitted stones. Wooden doors set with lever door knobs.

525.title: Common monsters
525.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IV – The Emperor: The Inverted Castle › Common monsters
525.body: Giggling Imps, Mummified Orcs, Orc Raiders, Sphinxes, Typhon Dogs, Scorpion Men, Dire Cats, Dire Beetles, Mummified Dragons

526.title: Dungeon lord
526.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IV – The Emperor: The Inverted Castle › Dungeon lord

527.title: V – The Hierophant: The City of Ruin
527.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › V – The Hierophant: The City of Ruin
527.body: Ruin is the name of the first City. Here, humanity first learned about the joys and terrors of being alive. The iconography of the place is full of the strength and beauty of youth. This is in sharp contrast to the current melancholy state of this level: dilapidated, derelict, and disfigured. During the first Crusades into the Underworld, it was discovered that the first City was plated with gold. Subsequent expeditions by adventuring guilds have stripped almost all gold from this dungeon level. Much of the remaining wealth is so large and unwieldy it would be difficult to extract. Ruin was pulled into the Underworld by His Majesty the Worm. His reasons are (as usual) enigmatic.

528.title: Sights
528.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › V – The Hierophant: The City of Ruin › Sights
528.body: Cyclopean structures tower above, once majestic but now fallen into ruin. Crumbling, colossal-sized statues of nameless rulers line the streets and crowd every square.

529.title: Sounds
529.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › V – The Hierophant: The City of Ruin › Sounds
529.body: A cold wind screams down the streets .

530.title: Smell and taste
530.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › V – The Hierophant: The City of Ruin › Smell and taste
530.body: The air is cold and dry as dust. Your breath frosts.

531.title: Lighting
531.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › V – The Hierophant: The City of Ruin › Lighting
531.body: Street lamps contain dire fireflies. These lamps shed a dull red glow, providing dim light in the streets. The ruined buildings are unlit and dark.

532.title: Structures
532.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › V – The Hierophant: The City of Ruin › Structures
532.body: The buildings are made of massive, closely-fitted granite stones. Most buildings are hollow, with floors and interiors rotted away. Occupied buildings have interiors constructed of scavenged masonry and furniture from other levels.

533.title: Common monsters
533.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › V – The Hierophant: The City of Ruin › Common monsters
533.body: Deconstruction Imps, Dire Cockroaches, Necrotic Slimes, Face Rats, Pacifist Werewolves, Animate Columns, Vampire Spawn, Harpies

534.title: Dungeon lord
534.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › V – The Hierophant: The City of Ruin › Dungeon lord

535.title: VI – The Lovers: The Pits
535.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VI – The Lovers: The Pits
535.body: If you think that the Underworld is merely the home of death, you are mistaken. It is teeming with life. In fact, that is one of the Underworld’s peculiar facets: death comes slowly here. One of the most animated levels of the Underworld is the Pits. The breeding ground for mutant albino ratmen, these tunnels are teeming with life. Quick lifecycles mean that generations are born, grow old, and die in the space of a week. The Rat King hosts blood sports in his filth-filled colosseum for his own amusement.

536.title: Sights
536.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VI – The Lovers: The Pits › Sights
536.body: Honeycombed holes in a natural cavern inspire trypophobia. They each ooze with pale slime, like a weeping sore. Below, a breeding pit swarming with bodies. A riot of flesh.

537.title: Sounds
537.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VI – The Lovers: The Pits › Sounds
537.body: A ceaseless chattering and squeaking and gnawing and chewing and scurrying.

538.title: Smell and taste
538.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VI – The Lovers: The Pits › Smell and taste
538.body: An almost unbearable acrid, ammonia reek .

539.title: Lighting
539.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VI – The Lovers: The Pits › Lighting
539.body: Ratmen use smoky torches to light their halls with dim light. Otherwise dark.

540.title: Structures
540.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VI – The Lovers: The Pits › Structures
540.body: Natural caverns and narrow tunnels, all slick with slimy mold and filth.

541.title: Common monsters
541.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VI – The Lovers: The Pits › Common monsters
541.body: Effluence Imps, Dire Lice, Ratmen, Goblins, Meat Slimes, Living Buboes, Zombie Troglodytes

542.title: Dungeon lord
542.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VI – The Lovers: The Pits › Dungeon lord

543.title: VII – The Chariot: Belly of the Beast
543.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VII – The Chariot: Belly of the Beast
543.body: The primordial world serpent Apep long gnawed upon the roots of the Underworld until he choked on the sins of the living and died. Now he’s stinking up the place. There are many things that the world serpent swallowed: monuments, tyrants, cathedrals, martyrs, magic swords, sailing galleys. They’re all lying in the serpent’s belly, ready to be reclaimed. It’s like somebody took a museum of pre-recorded history and shoved it into a series of reeking subway train cars made of meat. To enter this level, climb through Apep’s jaws (remember, even dead snakes can still bite) and crawl down the tunnel of its esophagus into its spacious stomach chambers.

544.title: Sights
544.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VII – The Chariot: Belly of the Beast › Sights
544.body: A litany of strange objects, from the miniscule to the monolithic, sits in about six inches of bile.

545.title: Sounds
545.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VII – The Chariot: Belly of the Beast › Sounds
545.body: The buzz of flies, the rumbling of digestion, and the slow dripping of fluids.

546.title: Smell and taste
546.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VII – The Chariot: Belly of the Beast › Smell and taste
546.body: A sweet stench, but not entirely rotten—akin to the formaldehyde-soaked frogs you dissected in high school.

547.title: Lighting
547.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VII – The Chariot: Belly of the Beast › Lighting

548.title: Structures
548.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VII – The Chariot: Belly of the Beast › Structures
548.body: Tunnel-like passages, usually about 15’ high and 15’ wide. Walls and ceilings are made of tissue and cartilage. Doors, such as they are, are valves and sphincters.

549.title: Common monsters
549.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VII – The Chariot: Belly of the Beast › Common monsters
549.body: Melancholic Imps, Dire Tapeworms, Dire Rats, Hellflies, Skeleton Jellies, Green Slimes, Various Stomach Prisoners

550.title: Dungeon lord
550.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VII – The Chariot: Belly of the Beast › Dungeon lord

551.title: VIII – Justice: The Drowned Wedding
551.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VIII – Justice: The Drowned Wedding
551.body: Everybody agrees that the wood elf princess Titikamook and the Finfolk King were lovers. Opinions differ as to whether the love was true or coerced. Everybody also agrees that Titikamook was to be married to her betrothed, the wood elf Kilium. What exactly happened at the wedding of these two elves is a matter of legend. It is said that the Finfolk King objected to the union, sunk the island, and turned the wedding guests into sea mammal monsters. The sunken island is preserved in a gigantic hollow pearl at the bottom of a subterranean lake. Getting there is nearly impossible without the aid of magic. Inside, although some sections are partially flooded, the air is breathable.

552.title: Sights
552.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VIII – Justice: The Drowned Wedding › Sights
552.body: An elven gala fallen into impossible age. Rotting food on the table. Half-drunk putrid glasses of wine. Decorations threading themselves into cobwebs.

553.title: Sounds
553.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VIII – Justice: The Drowned Wedding › Sounds
553.body: Moaning of ghosts. Distantly, the sound of music? The sound of water rushing in and out of cracks in the wall.

554.title: Smell and taste
554.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VIII – Justice: The Drowned Wedding › Smell and taste
554.body: A lingering smell of incense and rotting flowers. The ocean tang of the salty sea.

555.title: Lighting
555.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VIII – Justice: The Drowned Wedding › Lighting

556.title: Structures
556.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VIII – Justice: The Drowned Wedding › Structures
556.body: The surrounding pearl is diamond-hard and milky white. Structures on the island are made of wood, magically warped into shape.

557.title: Common monsters
557.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VIII – Justice: The Drowned Wedding › Common monsters
557.body: Brine Imps, Mermaids, Vodyanoy, Walrus Men, Land Whales, Dire Lice, Elephantine Oozes, Topiary Golems, Elven Ghosts, Draugr, Banshees

558.title: Dungeon lord
558.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › VIII – Justice: The Drowned Wedding › Dungeon lord

559.title: IX – The Hermit: The Library Heretical
559.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IX – The Hermit: The Library Heretical
559.body: Burning books create a heavy smoke that trickles down into the Underworld. The soot of this smoke is scraped and harvested by the ancient and unknowable cyclops librarians, who then painstakingly use it to restore the original uncensored texts. The culmination of their work lines the walls of the Library Heretical. It is said that the librarians do not understand the languages that they write, and are merely replicating the shapes embedded in the psychic residue. Still, as a result of their efforts, the Library Heretical contains a vast wealth of knowledge from every age of the Wide World.

560.title: Sights
560.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IX – The Hermit: The Library Heretical › Sights
560.body: Endless rows of books. Shelves stacked with scrolls. Sprawling scriptorium.

561.title: Sounds
561.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IX – The Hermit: The Library Heretical › Sounds
561.body: The scribbling of pens. The whisper of a turning page.

562.title: Smell and taste
562.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IX – The Hermit: The Library Heretical › Smell and taste
562.body: Dusty and dry. A lingering acrid smell of smoke.

563.title: Lighting
563.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IX – The Hermit: The Library Heretical › Lighting
563.body: Jars of dire fireflies hang from chains on the ceiling and provide bright light to most rooms. The jars are regularly tended by the librarians.

564.title: Structures
564.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IX – The Hermit: The Library Heretical › Structures
564.body: Corridors and rooms made of gigantic wooden bookshelves. Secret doors hidden in the bookshelves. Everything is sized for cyclopes: climbing up stairs is laborious for humans, like bouldering for underfolk.

565.title: Common monsters
565.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IX – The Hermit: The Library Heretical › Common monsters
565.body: Ink Imps, Cyclops Librarians, Origami Golems, Bookworms, Crawling Brains, Book Mimics, Memetic Plagues, Speech Bubble Jellyfish

566.title: Dungeon lord
566.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › IX – The Hermit: The Library Heretical › Dungeon lord

567.title: X – The Wheel of Fortune: The Field of Reeds
567.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › X – The Wheel of Fortune: The Field of Reeds
567.body: At the confluence of the five rivers of the Underworld is the Field of Reeds, a marshy swamp choked with the detritus that’s washed down from upper levels. The terrain is treacherous: seemingly solid ground suddenly gives way to sucking pits. There are soft grasses that turn blade-sharp when agitated. Huge mangrove trees create small islands that knit together the flooded space, but even they are fickle. They whisper and conspire with each other, passing along rumors and muttering about grudges. It’s said that the waters of the Underworld rivers have strange properties. Do not drink from them.

568.title: Sights
568.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › X – The Wheel of Fortune: The Field of Reeds › Sights
568.body: A Louisiana swamp at night. The eyeshine of scrambling things disappearing into the mud, hiding themselves from the light of your torch. Thick webs of vines connecting jagged tree stumps. A thousand shades of green.

569.title: Sounds
569.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › X – The Wheel of Fortune: The Field of Reeds › Sounds
569.body: The soft plop of something leaping into the water. The whine of insects.

570.title: Smell and taste
570.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › X – The Wheel of Fortune: The Field of Reeds › Smell and taste
570.body: The fetid water smells like fever sweats: hot and wet and insomniac.

571.title: Lighting
571.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › X – The Wheel of Fortune: The Field of Reeds › Lighting
571.body: Parts of the swamps are continuously on fire. Otherwise, all is dark.

572.title: Structures
572.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › X – The Wheel of Fortune: The Field of Reeds › Structures
572.body: Crumbling stone ruins, looming up out of the swamps.

573.title: Common monsters
573.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › X – The Wheel of Fortune: The Field of Reeds › Common monsters
573.body: Brine Imps, Will o’ Wisps, Bog Mummies, Dire Spiders, Dire Toads, Hydrae, Harpies, Ogres

574.title: Dungeon lord
574.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › X – The Wheel of Fortune: The Field of Reeds › Dungeon lord

575.title: XI – Strength: The Sepulcher of Titans
575.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XI – Strength: The Sepulcher of Titans
575.body: Philosophers have speculated that humans were not the first people to govern where the City now stands. The Sepulcher of Titans supports these attestations. Here, the bodies of gigantic creatures lie in unquiet repose. The titans are not dead, merely dismembered. Their decapitated heads sit silently, thinking and watching. If you hooked a bellows up to their neck to give them breath, they could still talk their ancient language. If their giant arms are freed from their coffins, they crawl around blindly, looking for their bodies. If you pull their hearts from their canopic jars, you’ll find them still beating. (Do not under any circumstances eat the titans’ flesh.)

576.title: Sights
576.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XI – Strength: The Sepulcher of Titans › Sights
576.body: The hallways are close-fitting, as if a secondary prison to the dismembered giants. Humans walk down them with a claustrophobic feeling. These narrow hallways open up into vaulted chambers that prominently display the burial chambers of muslin-wrapped giants.

577.title: Sounds
577.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XI – Strength: The Sepulcher of Titans › Sounds
577.body: A hallowed quiet broken by the occasional rustling from within the stone tombs as the giants resettle themselves.

578.title: Smell and taste
578.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XI – Strength: The Sepulcher of Titans › Smell and taste
578.body: The cool scent of damp earth. A pungent scent of mold.

579.title: Lighting
579.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XI – Strength: The Sepulcher of Titans › Lighting

580.title: Structures
580.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XI – Strength: The Sepulcher of Titans › Structures
580.body: The rooms are made of unworked stone fitted closely together without cement. The hallways are made of natural caverns. Occasional stone doors of gigantic size separate chambers; difficult to move but unlocked.

581.title: Common monsters
581.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XI – Strength: The Sepulcher of Titans › Common monsters
581.body: Tunneling Imps, Ogres, Mummified Giants, Disembodied Crawling Hands, Furies, Dire Spiders, Chimerae, Manticores

582.title: Dungeon lord
582.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XI – Strength: The Sepulcher of Titans › Dungeon lord

583.title: XII – The Hanged Man: Xania
583.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XII – The Hanged Man: Xania
583.body: When the first human died, it took everybody by surprise. As necromancers furiously tried to solve the problem of eternal life, one sorceress took a bold new approach. This sorceress had a daughter and named her Xania. She named them all Xania. Through magic, she cloned her daughter thousands upon thousands of times. The sorceress automated these processes, and has long since perished. The processes continue. Xania survives. In an enchanted tower in the Underworld, magical cloning labs work continuously to unstitch and reweave the same person, over and over. There are hundreds of Xanias. Some are saner than others, but none are particularly sane. At least, not how humans think of it.

584.title: Sights
584.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XII – The Hanged Man: Xania › Sights
584.body: The most common material in this dungeon level is human flesh. Tapestries are woven of human hair. Books are bound in human skin. Furniture is made out of human bones. Meals are made out of—you guessed it! (Xanias do not think of this as weird. It’s a little like masturbation, maybe.)

585.title: Sounds
585.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XII – The Hanged Man: Xania › Sounds
585.body: The sounds of a working castle: women gossiping, the crying of babies, the birth-sacs filling with liquid, nightsoil being emptied, floors being swept, etc.

586.title: Smell and taste
586.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XII – The Hanged Man: Xania › Smell and taste
586.body: It smells like a birthing room .

587.title: Lighting
587.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XII – The Hanged Man: Xania › Lighting
587.body: Candelabras of human-fat candles provide bright light to most rooms. Hallways are dark.

588.title: Structures
588.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XII – The Hanged Man: Xania › Structures
588.body: The rooms are made of crumbling stone. Doors are made of metal. Locked doors are heavily reinforced. Furniture is strangely well-made, though in an Ed Gein pastiche.

589.title: Common monsters
589.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XII – The Hanged Man: Xania › Common monsters

590.title: Dungeon lord
590.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XII – The Hanged Man: Xania › Dungeon lord

591.title: XIII – Death: The Necropolis of Ot
591.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIII – Death: The Necropolis of Ot
591.body: When the first human died, it took everybody by surprise. Nobody knew that would happen. Life had seemed to be eternal. Nobody could remember a time before being alive, and nobody had yet conceived of a time after being alive. The revelation that they would someday die terrified the first City. To solve this problem, humanity sought the aid of sorcery. Unfortunately, sorcery is a sword without a hilt: there’s no safe way to hold it. The result of the first City’s invention of necromancy is the Necropolis of Ot.

592.title: Sights
592.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIII – Death: The Necropolis of Ot › Sights
592.body: A city of the dead governed by the dead. Pyramids of bone rise up in a mammoth cavern, ringed by walls of heaped skulls. Funerary urns, carved with the likeness of life, clutter the corners of every chamber and hallway.

593.title: Sounds
593.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIII – Death: The Necropolis of Ot › Sounds
593.body: The dead whisper and mutter ceaselessly, but you can never catch exactly what they’re saying.

594.title: Smell and taste
594.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIII – Death: The Necropolis of Ot › Smell and taste
594.body: It is dry as dust. Your lips are chapped.

595.title: Lighting
595.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIII – Death: The Necropolis of Ot › Lighting

596.title: Structures
596.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIII – Death: The Necropolis of Ot › Structures
596.body: The buildings of the necropolis are made of limestone, lined and decorated with millions of human bones. Doors are made of stone set on fulcrums at their center point, allowing them to easily turn.

597.title: Common monsters
597.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIII – Death: The Necropolis of Ot › Common monsters
597.body: Saprovore Imps, Ghosts, Zombies, Skeletons, Wraiths, Shadows, Skin Slimes, Tooth Fairies, Dire Owls, Monstrance Golems

598.title: Dungeon lord
598.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIII – Death: The Necropolis of Ot › Dungeon lord

599.title: XIV – Temperance: The Menagerie of Singular Creatures
599.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIV – Temperance: The Menagerie of Singular Creatures
599.body: The sphinxes whisper of a time before there were multitudinous species—droves of oxen, murmurations of starlings, schools of fish, prides of lions. Before that, there was only His Majesty the Worm. In His loneliness, He dipped his claws into the Well of Souls and brought forth singular creatures. Things unique, with no others of their kind. These things were subsequently forbidden from the Wide World, and so have been trapped in the Underworld. Each chamber is home to a thing utterly unique, with unique treasure, a uniquely sad story, and a unique danger.

600.title: Sights
600.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIV – Temperance: The Menagerie of Singular Creatures › Sights
600.body: Moving from the Dajjal’s room to the Simurgh’s room is like moving from night to day. The gloomy caverns give way to a vaulted room lit with a crystalline pillar shining like the sun. The white roots of weirwood trees provide the Simurgh a roost. On the far wall, heavy chains forbid egress to the Tarasque’s chamber.

601.title: Sounds
601.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIV – Temperance: The Menagerie of Singular Creatures › Sounds
601.body: Various. The dolorous sound of Echidna’s glass organ is never far away.

602.title: Smell and taste
602.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIV – Temperance: The Menagerie of Singular Creatures › Smell and taste
602.body: Various. Each room has a particular odor .

603.title: Lighting
603.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIV – Temperance: The Menagerie of Singular Creatures › Lighting
603.body: Various. Some rooms are dark, some are well lit.

604.title: Structures
604.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIV – Temperance: The Menagerie of Singular Creatures › Structures
604.body: Various. The majority of the rooms are caverns of unworked stone, though different creatures have special structures designed to comfort their peculiar shapes.

605.title: Common monsters
605.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIV – Temperance: The Menagerie of Singular Creatures › Common monsters

606.title: Dungeon lord
606.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIV – Temperance: The Menagerie of Singular Creatures › Dungeon lord

607.title: XV – The Devil: The Hellmarkt
607.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XV – The Devil: The Hellmarkt
607.body: The Hellmarkt sits at a crossroads between the Underworld and the far realms, where spirits dwell. It takes human commerce and turns it up a notch. Spirits trade intangible things: the color of your eyes, the memory of your mother, your sense of fear. In return? They give you (almost) anything you want. It is impossible to buy your heart’s desire. However, many spirits have powerful tools that would make achieving your quest much simpler. They are willing to trade these things to you for a price. The costs of the Hellmarkt seem reasonable. Too reasonable. Alas, no mortal has ever made this bargain and avoided regret.

608.title: Sights
608.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XV – The Devil: The Hellmarkt › Sights
608.body: Goblins cluster, offering you a variety of pretty, cheap things. A myriad of spirits eagerly sing structures into existence: there are a thousand details to take in at once, and the spirits insist that you pay attention to everything.

609.title: Sounds
609.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XV – The Devil: The Hellmarkt › Sounds
609.body: Inhuman glossolalia babbles from all sides; two spirits argue about minute differences in their contrasting epistemological eschatologies. When they glimpse you, they are excited. “Come by! Come buy!”

610.title: Smell and taste
610.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XV – The Devil: The Hellmarkt › Smell and taste
610.body: Each stall has a different intoxicating scent prickling at the memory centers of your brain: cut grass, your mother’s perfume, the food on your wedding day.

611.title: Lighting
611.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XV – The Devil: The Hellmarkt › Lighting
611.body: Well lit with fires of many colors .

612.title: Structures
612.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XV – The Devil: The Hellmarkt › Structures
612.body: A huge cavern has been co-opted into a huge outdoor market. Bedouin-like tents define the stalls. Most rooms and pathways are defined only by silks and tapestries.

613.title: Common monsters
613.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XV – The Devil: The Hellmarkt › Common monsters
613.body: Servitor Imps, Elf Cloneslugs, Angels, Devils, Genii, Daemons, Goblins, Dream Fairies

614.title: Dungeon lords
614.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XV – The Devil: The Hellmarkt › Dungeon lords

615.title: XVI – The Tower: The House of Many Angles
615.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVI – The Tower: The House of Many Angles
615.body: The Underworld is the cradle and grave of all things, including concepts. Like Plato’s theory of forms, the Underworld births ideaspace—the manifestation of physical forms in their most idealized shape. The idea of buildings was first had by the Underworld, and in its dark dreams, the germ has taken root and spread into an infestation of hallways, a riot of walls, flowering gables, and endless chambers. Unburdened by the constraints of reality, the House of Many Angles folds and unfolds itself like an origami castle. Hallways loop impossibly into each other. Changing the geometry of a single room might change the shape of the entire complex.

616.title: Sights
616.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVI – The Tower: The House of Many Angles › Sights
616.body: Architecture of a thousand different styles all jammed together. Rooms are laid out in improbable ways, like they were designed by H. H. Holmes.

617.title: Sounds
617.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVI – The Tower: The House of Many Angles › Sounds
617.body: The acoustics of the rooms are at once beautiful and strange. If your companions whisper on the far side of the room, you can clearly hear it, but there’s a sense of yawning space above you that feels crippling. Occasional grinding sounds hint that, when unobserved, other rooms in the House are rearranging themselves.

618.title: Smell and taste
618.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVI – The Tower: The House of Many Angles › Smell and taste

619.title: Lighting
619.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVI – The Tower: The House of Many Angles › Lighting

620.title: Structures
620.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVI – The Tower: The House of Many Angles › Structures
620.body: There is no consistency between chambers. Some are made of sturdy pine wood painted black. Some are rough-hewn logs of extinct trees. Some are made of fitted stones.

621.title: Common monsters
621.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVI – The Tower: The House of Many Angles › Common monsters
621.body: Deconstruction Imps, Gargoyles, Dire Centipedes, Prolapsedogs, Inverted Horses, Face Rats, Non- Euclidean Snakes

622.title: Dungeon lord
622.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVI – The Tower: The House of Many Angles › Dungeon lord

623.title: XVII – The Star: The Augury
623.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVII – The Star: The Augury
623.body: The clockwork mechanisms that define the Augury exceed contemporary science. It’s like the Antikythera mechanism taken to a castle scale, with rooms of gears and cogs housed by limestone walls. Its intended purpose is bafflingly obscure. The only signifying elements are found in three separate orreries, which depict detailed but utterly alien skyscapes. However, clever dungeon denizens and adventurers have found many seemingly unintended uses for the Augury. Time seems especially fickle here. Food doesn’t spoil, but molds grow quickly. Hours seem to pass in minutes. Bright light causes paper to act photoreactive, capturing shadow imprints. Is this obscure mechanism responsible for the strange temporal features of the Underworld?

624.title: Sights
624.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVII – The Star: The Augury › Sights
624.body: A tower housing a large, slowly rotating flywheel with four chain-bound counterweights.

625.title: Sounds
625.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVII – The Star: The Augury › Sounds
625.body: Loud whirring and clicking, like a huge grandfather clock. Echoes of past conversations reverberate back down the halls.

626.title: Smell and taste
626.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVII – The Star: The Augury › Smell and taste

627.title: Lighting
627.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVII – The Star: The Augury › Lighting

628.title: Structures
628.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVII – The Star: The Augury › Structures
628.body: The structures are all centered around and intended to support a building-sized computational machine of bronze clockwork gears. Hallways and chambers made of wood. Walls are plastered. Arched wooden doors with round door knobs.

629.title: Common monsters
629.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVII – The Star: The Augury › Common monsters
629.body: Clockwork Imps, Clockwork Knights, Intelligent Mice, Blood Mists, Degenerate Dwarves, Oil Elementals

630.title: Dungeon lord
630.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVII – The Star: The Augury › Dungeon lord

631.title: XVIII – The Moon: The Truesilver Forge
631.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVIII – The Moon: The Truesilver Forge
631.body: Although the supply chain and logistics are impossible to manage, a colony of underfolk have settled near this lode in an attempt to try and mine it. Unfortunately, mithril mining is incredibly unhealthy. Though mining has made the Truesilver Forge colony rich, it has also made them deeply disturbed. They’re suspicious and suffer hallucinations. Anybody who spends too long on this level begins to suffer these effects as well. Sorcerers should note that mithril increases the potency of magic (kind of like nega-iron). The presence of so much mithril at this level has strange, unpredictable effects on spells.

632.title: Sights
632.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVIII – The Moon: The Truesilver Forge › Sights
632.body: Veins of mithril glow dully in the rock. A thin river of molten lava bifurcates the level, feeding into an elaborate stone trench to heat a dwarf-made forge.

633.title: Sounds
633.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVIII – The Moon: The Truesilver Forge › Sounds
633.body: The tireless falling of mattocks and shovels. Blast furnaces roaring. An argument, a wet thud, hysterical laughter mixed with weeping.

634.title: Smell and taste
634.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVIII – The Moon: The Truesilver Forge › Smell and taste

635.title: Lighting
635.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVIII – The Moon: The Truesilver Forge › Lighting
635.body: Chambers are lit 50% of the time with red-glass lamps. Hallways are unlit.

636.title: Structures
636.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVIII – The Moon: The Truesilver Forge › Structures
636.body: Man-made tunnels that connect natural caverns. Inconsistent, sloped flooring. Wooden supports hold weak ceilings up; wooden bridges span gaps.

637.title: Common monsters
637.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVIII – The Moon: The Truesilver Forge › Common monsters
637.body: Hallucination Imps, Argyric Underfolk, Quicksilver Slimes, Dire Ants, Mutant Canaries

638.title: Dungeon lord
638.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XVIII – The Moon: The Truesilver Forge › Dungeon lord

639.title: XIX – The Sun: The White Gardens
639.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIX – The Sun: The White Gardens
639.body: In the sunless reaches, light has taken on strange forms. Bizarre breeds of mushrooms have learned to shed illumination as white and cold as the stars. The light lures creatures into the sprawling groves of fungi who quickly become addled, poisoned, and lost. Their bodies go on to provide nutrients to the White Gardens. The White Gardens are fields of dungeon mushrooms growing in a series of natural caverns. Some of the mushrooms are so soft and small that they resemble translucent grass covering the subterranean floor. Others are tuberous and as large as trees. Still others still have a dim cunning and hate the rival kingdoms of plants, animals, and bacteria.

640.title: Sights
640.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIX – The Sun: The White Gardens › Sights
640.body: Caverns vary wildly in size, swelling to the size of cathedrals and contracting to unnavigable seams through the stone. On almost every surface, fungi resembling sea anemones wave their spongy polyps.

641.title: Sounds
641.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIX – The Sun: The White Gardens › Sounds
641.body: The drip of water. The occasional hiss of a mushroom releasing its spores.

642.title: Smell and taste
642.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIX – The Sun: The White Gardens › Smell and taste
642.body: The air is damp. There’s a pungent earthy smell. Clouds of spores smell fishy and taste like mustard.

643.title: Lighting
643.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIX – The Sun: The White Gardens › Lighting
643.body: Bioluminescent mushrooms shed LED-white light . This counts as bright light .

644.title: Structures
644.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIX – The Sun: The White Gardens › Structures
644.body: The cavern’s walls and floors are the consistency of pocked corral. The corral is a bone-white color.

645.title: Common monsters
645.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIX – The Sun: The White Gardens › Common monsters
645.body: Spore-choked Imps, Fungoids, Dire Crabs, Shrieker Mushrooms, Polytechnic Polyspores, Spore Zombies

646.title: Dungeon lord
646.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XIX – The Sun: The White Gardens › Dungeon lord

647.title: XX – Judgement: The Dragonbone Memorial
647.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XX – Judgement: The Dragonbone Memorial
647.body: When humans stole the Well of Souls, the dragon city of Night crumbled away into dust. In the span of ages since, dragons have painstakingly remade the city out of the bones of their dead in the Underworld. Why? Nobody knows. Nobody knows anything about how or why dragons do anything. Orcs call this city the Dragonbone Memorial. A sect of religious fanatic orcs believes the Dragonbone Memorial to be their promised land. There is inter-factional disagreement about whether they should lead the orcish nations down into the Underworld or move the dragonbone city up to the surface piece by piece.

648.title: Sights
648.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XX – Judgement: The Dragonbone Memorial › Sights
648.body: Narrow streets suddenly give way to a spacious square. A fountain depicts a serpent devouring its own tail. The fountain is full of blood.

649.title: Sounds
649.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XX – Judgement: The Dragonbone Memorial › Sounds
649.body: Dripping water. Very distantly, chimes like a Tibetan bowl. An ominous rumbling seems to be coming from somewhere below.

650.title: Smell and taste
650.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XX – Judgement: The Dragonbone Memorial › Smell and taste
650.body: The lingering haze of an electrical fire .

651.title: Lighting
651.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XX – Judgement: The Dragonbone Memorial › Lighting
651.body: Although some creatures (like goblins and orcs) carry torches, the memorial itself provides no sources of light.

652.title: Structures
652.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XX – Judgement: The Dragonbone Memorial › Structures
652.body: The walls of the city are dry-stack bones. The roads are paved with crushed oyster shells. Buildings are composed of colossal, fossilized creatures reshaped into ancient architecture, each room no longer serving a meaningful purpose. Doors are made of fossilized wood.

653.title: Common monsters
653.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XX – Judgement: The Dragonbone Memorial › Common monsters
653.body: Keening Imps, Goblins, Orc Cultists, Human Crusaders, Bloody Cruciforms, Shadows, Panthers, Sword Spiders, Dire Rats, Dragon Skeletons, Dragons

654.title: Dungeon lord
654.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XX – Judgement: The Dragonbone Memorial › Dungeon lord

655.title: XXI – The World: The Undertomb
655.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XXI – The World: The Undertomb
655.body: At the center of the Underworld is the Undertomb. At the center of the Undertomb is the Well of Souls, the font of all life and death. It is filled with vaults and chambers. Each room is imbued with symbols of religious allegory. Nobody understands the allegory or knows what the symbolism means. When unobserved, the paths between the chambers re-architect themselves. Light is blasphemous in the Undertomb, where darkness must forever reign supreme. Fire gutters as if frightened, and the circle of your torchlight seems to be several inches smaller than normal.

656.title: Sights
656.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XXI – The World: The Undertomb › Sights
656.body: Hewn, fitted stones seem to be devolving into a cavernous space. Strange images flecked with gold are worked into the stone: A lamb with a human face. The castration of a bull. A man crowned with an ouroboros.

657.title: Sounds
657.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XXI – The World: The Undertomb › Sounds
657.body: The air here feels like a breath. Sometimes pushing, sometimes pulling. A yawning feeling.

658.title: Smell and taste
658.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XXI – The World: The Undertomb › Smell and taste
658.body: The air is warm and sulfurous. It smells and tastes like rotten eggs.

659.title: Lighting
659.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XXI – The World: The Undertomb › Lighting

660.title: Structures
660.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XXI – The World: The Undertomb › Structures
660.body: Chambers consist of caverns hewn from partially worked stone. The doors are made of metal, and many have very complex locking mechanisms.

661.title: Common monsters
661.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XXI – The World: The Undertomb › Common monsters
661.body: Katabatic Imps, Ogre Spiders, Statuary Golems, Skeleton Jellies, Lost Adventurers Undergoing Apotheosis, Disassembling Angels, Goblins, Dragons

662.title: Dungeon lord
662.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › XXI – The World: The Undertomb › Dungeon lord

663.title: Creating interesting rooms
663.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms
663.body: The basic procedure for populating a dungeon is this: Come up with a bunch of interesting ideas and write them down. This is just as easy and hard as it sounds. Using the principles for creating interesting room descriptions (Write Room Descriptions), add features to each room. Some example features and inspiration for creating your own are provided below. There are twenty-one of them, so you can flip over a major arcana card to quickly select one if you desire randomness.

664.title: 1. Circle of power
664.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 1. Circle of power
664.body: Sites of power constructed where the leylines of the dungeon converge. These circles are designed as gates between the realm of Flesh and the far realms—either to bar outside entities or beckon such entities in. They are dangerous things, whose magic is more than any single mortal sorcerer can master.

665.title: Example
665.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 1. Circle of power › Example
665.body: A glyph written on the floor crackles with obviously discordant magical energy. The glyph is surrounded by five, five-sided pyramidal stones. The side of each stone is marked with runes that read “AB-RA-KA-DAB-RA”. If the guild steps onto the glyph without changing the arrangement of the stones, they are teleported to a deeper level of the dungeon and turned inside out (instant death). The glyph must be harmonized by turning the pyramidal stones so the runes facing the inside of the glyph read “Abrakadabra.” This word can start from any stone, but should proceed in order until every syllable is used sequentially in a clockwise manner. When this is done, the teleportation magic is safe to use.

666.title: 2. Altar
666.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 2. Altar
666.body: An altar is a table intended for sacrifice. Altars are shaped in the semblance of the god to which they are dedicated. It is a conduit to a higher power, and prayers to the appropriate divinity carry more weight here.

667.title: Example
667.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 2. Altar › Example
667.body: The altar of the Black Goat is a table shaped like a standing she-goat, her back forming the flat surface of the table. On it, candles have burned down into wax puddles atop goat skulls. It is blood stained. A sacrifice of a living creature on this altar has a 1-in-4 chance to cure any afflictions. If the celebrants have multiple afflictions, test each one to see if it is cured.

668.title: 3. Cage
668.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 3. Cage
668.body: A prison, a hanging gibbet, a jail designed to constrain its prisoners. What crimes could they have committed to be bound to such a fate? Are they imprisoned unjustly or have they committed sins that cannot be forgiven?

669.title: Example
669.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 3. Cage › Example
669.body: A hanging cage made of thin sticks lashed together with leather cords. The door is fastened simply with a knot of herb (monkshood). The cage looks like you could kick it apart easily. Inside, an old man named Zacchaeus claims to have been brought here as food for vampires and begs to be let out. In truth, Zacchaeus is a werewolf. The monkshood (otherwise known as wolfsbane) keeps him so weak he cannot break the bars.

670.title: 4. Throne
670.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 4. Throne
670.body: The thrones of the former rulers of the Underworld still contain some power. Those who sit on them are given a measure of control over a certain dungeon feature or a special awareness of a facet of the Underworld. However, thrones often possess magical curses or traps laid on them to ensure only the worthy sit upon them.

671.title: Example
671.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 4. Throne › Example
671.body: A colossal throne covered in dust, mice skeletons, and owl droppings. The back of the throne is sculpted like spread owl wings. The arms of the throne each depict a closed eye. Sitting on the throne while holding a light source causes it to suddenly flare and go out. The adventurer must succeed in a test of Wands or be Blinded until after the next Camp Phase. Those who sit on the throne find their hearing greatly improved. Immediately, they hear the whistling of wind through a crack in a secret door on the north wall. Additionally, they hear whispering far above them. If they stay seated for an entire watch, they can hear one rumor spoken by someone distantly in the dungeon.

672.title: 5. Idol
672.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 5. Idol
672.body: The Underworld contains giant idols of strange gods. Some say they were raised by ancient troglodytes. Some say they were gods that crawled into the veins of the earth and became fossils. In either event, there is still power in these colossi.

673.title: Example
673.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 5. Idol › Example
673.body: A giant statue of a seated devil with gemstone eyes. It holds a huge brazier of coals. Attempting to pry out the idol’s gemstone eyes causes the idol to tip the brazier over, pouring liquid fire into the room. The room’s floor becomes lava. The would-be thieves are trapped on the statue with no obvious way out.

674.title: 6. Library
674.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 6. Library
674.body: Books and scrolls are hoarded by scholars, lore-masters, and wizards. Libraries house books that are written on papyrus, vellum, and wax tablets. Many things that are forgotten on the surface can be found trapped in letters here. However, it takes time to carefully pour over the tomes here, translating the antique dialects and shepherding the fragile pages.

675.title: Example
675.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 6. Library › Example
675.body: The necromancer Crabbe made the Library of Heads: mummified heads sitting on concentric shelves in a circular room. If you pick up the heads and blow through their neck hole, they begin to recite their life’s story in their native tongue. There are 102 heads here. Many have nothing interesting to say to an adventurer. A few hold some esoteric knowledge worthy of a researcher in a niche subject. At least three were rival sorcerers who speak eloquently about their forays into the far realms.

676.title: 7. Elevator
676.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 7. Elevator
676.body: Elevators are platforms or chambers that move around the dungeon (vertically, horizontally, or in stranger ways). Different levels of the Underworld may be connected by elevators that need to be activated.

677.title: Example
677.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 7. Elevator › Example
677.body: The guild steps into the bottom of a deep pit. A colossal chain ending in a huge hook dangles from an unseen place high above. A giant earthworm is pierced by the hook, wiggly feebly. If the guild manages to make a significant pull on the chain, the giant at the top of the pit pulls the hook and chain up to the upper level. He’s not interested in the guild and will discard them at this upper level as being “under his limit.”

678.title: 8. Hearthfire
678.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 8. Hearthfire
678.body: This place looks safe enough for now. Here, other adventuring guilds have encamped. An ember of their fire remains. Light it again to kindle some hope in this dark place.

679.title: Example
679.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 8. Hearthfire › Example
679.body: A small shrine with a campfire in which a ruined sword has been driven. Those who camp here restore all Resolve without having to burn charged Bonds.

680.title: 9. Merchant
680.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 9. Merchant
680.body: Rule of Acquisition 34: War is good for business. Adventurers are a desperate sort, and their pockets are weighed down with grave goods, golden idols, and other ill-gotten gains. Shrewd merchants have learned that you can make more selling a single candle to an adventurer in a dark dungeon than you can selling candles to a cotter’s wife all year. That said, most merchants you find in a dungeon aren’t the sort to go in for a brick-and-mortar business.

681.title: Example
681.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 9. Merchant › Example
681.body: Grinnin’ Grimnir is a goblin who hauls around a sleigh filled with assorted goods. He always sells balls of twine (1 gold), candles (5 gold), torches (10 gold), daggers (20 gold), and rations (30 gold). He also has ten random items every time you encounter him. Put him on your Meatgrinder. Grinnin’ Grimnir is protected by a curse. Anyone who kills him will be cursed with vile luck for a year. For an adventurer, this spells certain death. Those who try to run away from the bad luck in remote townships undergo so much trauma they eventually resemble a little, constantly-giggling goblin. They are eventually seized with the strange compulsion to load up a sleigh and start a little trade in the Underworld.

682.title: 10. Machine
682.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 10. Machine
682.body: Mechanisms made by ancient hands, the purpose and the logic of which are not known. Some machines are malfunctioning, producing imperfect results. Some are broken, but can be fixed (though not understood) by replacing an obvious part or providing a power source. Some work perfectly, but exactly what they do and why is beyond mortal ken.

683.title: Example
683.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 10. Machine › Example
683.body: The workings of the Unmaking Machine are hidden inside its body, which resembles a 40’ x 40’ x 40’ cube. The first time the Unmaking Machine is encountered by the guild, there is a single, six inch, cube-shaped section missing from the left side of the cube. This missing cube can be found elsewhere in the dungeon and inserted into it like a key. The machine thereafter begins to function. Once repaired, the only interface with which to operate the machine are two apertures, both square holes exactly 13” in diameter, both on the cube’s “front.” When an item is placed into the upper hole, it slides into the darkness as if drawn in by a hand. The cube emits a series of grinding sounds. Then, the component construction materials of the item issue out from the lower hole. For example, if a sword was put into the top hole, the cube emits the following: an ingot of iron, small cubes of trace minerals involved in embellishment, a strip of leather and a solid block of wood (both from the hilt), a dollop of animal-based glue, and a single droplet of oil (residual from maintenance). If an item is jammed into the lower hole, it comes out of the top hole terribly mangled.

684.title: 11. False tomb
684.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 11. False tomb
684.body: There are tombs down here. But there are also false tombs intended to baffle and punish grave robbers. These facades obscure the true burial chambers behind secret doors and deadly traps.

685.title: Example
685.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 11. False tomb › Example
685.body: A mosaic depicts a bull-headed man holding a scale with a feather and a heart. Beneath it, two doors. Ancient writing on the wall (when translated) reads: “The just enter on the left to pass to paradise. The unjust enter to the right to meet their punishment.” The doors both lead to the same small chamber. About five seconds after the doors are opened, a two-ton block drops into the small chamber, crushing anyone within who doesn’t succeed in a test of Pentacles to dodge back into the false tomb.

686.title: 12. Magic wall
686.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 12. Magic wall
686.body: Magical barriers may be raised to gate certain sections of a dungeon. These could be magical force fields or walls made of esoteric energies, such as walls of fire or walls of ice. The key to these walls are almost always magical. Often, the artifact or structure generating the wall needs to be disabled.

687.title: Example
687.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 12. Magic wall › Example
687.body: An archway of skulls bifurcates a room. The keystone skull once belonged to a giant bird. A malicious presence haunts the bird skull, whose evil will only allows those who bear the tokens of its master the Pigeon King to pass. This is not a physical barrier but a mental command screaming DO NOT ENTER. It cannot be resisted by any sentient, living creature. Arrows and spells may pass under the archway. The keystone skull’s evil will can only work on creatures it can see. Blinding the skull (with a Flare spell) or sneaking past while Shrouded will also allow passage.

688.title: 13. Sepulcher
688.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 13. Sepulcher
688.body: Past the false tombs, sepulchers entomb the dead. Sometimes these dead are restless, sometimes they have withered away to bones. Adventurers low in scruples and funds sometimes loot these sepulchers in hopes of grave goods, but find traps and curses instead.

689.title: Example
689.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 13. Sepulcher › Example
689.body: A sarcophagus whose stone lid depicts a snake-headed human. The lid is massively heavy and can only be moved with a combined strength of five adventurers; tools like a ten-foot pole used as a lever double an adventurer’s lifting capacity, but usually snap the lever unless it is unusually sturdy. Inside, a mummy. The mummy is just a normal mummy, not undead. It does carry a disease, however. If you handle the body directly without gloves, test Cups to avoid contracting the mummy rot affliction. The wrappings around the mummy are a treasure map. Mark a hidden room on the guild’s map of this dungeon level, in which treasure can be found.

690.title: 14. Fountain
690.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 14. Fountain
690.body: Fountains in the Underworld are usually enchanted. Drinking, bathing, or dipping items into the fountain activates their enchantments.

691.title: Example
691.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 14. Fountain › Example
691.body: A merry face is carved on the outlet of the spring where this fountain flows. The face speaks simple phrases, welcoming travelers to drink from its waters. Drinking from the waters causes mild euphoria and hallucinations. If under any persistent negative enchantments, geasa, mind control, or similar effects, adventurers who drink the water are allowed to test Wands to attempt to overcome them. However, adventurers who have drunk from the water must play their lowest card for Initiative during Challenges and cannot cast spells due to consistent giggling interrupting their incantations. This effect lasts until the Camp Phase.

692.title: 15. Statue
692.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 15. Statue
692.body: These graven images bear the semblance of ancient kings, heroes, and mythological figures. They reflect the culture of those who shaped them, and provide clues to their creator’s worldview with regards to the local dungeon level. A recent poll of dungeon delvers found that 70% of puzzles incorporated statues in some way.

693.title: Example
693.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 15. Statue › Example
693.body: A three-faced statue of the elven Tripartite—the Maiden, the Mother, and the Crone—stands in the middle of a triangular room. Examination of the statue reveals scratch marks on the floor near its base, indicating the statue has been turned from its original position. Two of the walls of the room are decorated with mosaics. One bears a crescent moon. One bears a white circle. The third wall is blank. If the statue is turned so the Maiden faces the crescent moon, the Mother faces the white circle, and the Crone faces the blank wall, the blank wall will become a misty portal that will teleport the guild to a new location.

694.title: 16. Oubliette
694.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 16. Oubliette
694.body: An oubliette is where you put someone to forget about them. Accessed only by a trapdoor, these deep pits serve as prisons for those now long abandoned.

695.title: Example
695.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 16. Oubliette › Example
695.body: This oubliette contains two skeletons: one of a human (wearing the tattered remains of a once-fabulous gown) and one of a dwarf. The human skeleton has tooth marks indicative of a cannibalistic end. Instructions are written on the wall in blood to find a secret door elsewhere on this dungeon level.

696.title: 17. Mirror
696.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 17. Mirror
696.body: Magical mirrors create aberrant reflections of the real world. They sometimes serve as traps, creating doppelgangers of the adventurers. They might serve as portals, perhaps to an alternate dimension. These also might be the focal piece of a puzzle, where the mirror must reflect a ray of light in a different direction.

697.title: Example
697.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 17. Mirror › Example
697.body: A hall of twelve mirrors, three of which bear the frozen visage of an adventurer and three of which are broken. Those who look into an empty mirror see their own reflection frozen there. Adventurers who look into an empty mirror create a “save state.” At any point, they can choose to reset their bodies directly to this point—same XP, same Wounds, same equipment, etc. This must be done consciously, i.e., before they are unconscious or dead. When this ability is activated, the image disappears from the mirror and the mirror breaks.

698.title: 18. Painting
698.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 18. Painting
698.body: Paintings, tapestries, frescoes, and mosaics provide more than simple dungeon decoration. They often hide secrets, carry an enchantment, or provide important context to nearby puzzles.

699.title: Example
699.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 18. Painting › Example
699.body: A framed painting of a door with no knob. Elsewhere in the dungeon are magical paints. Painting a knob onto the door will turn the painting into a functioning secret door.

700.title: 19. River
700.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 19. River
700.body: Adventurers beware! Underworld rivers notoriously have uncanny properties, and drinking even a drop of their water will rob you of your memories, plunge you into eternal sleep, cause ceaseless weeping, or deliver other terrible curses. Underground rivers initially serve as barriers that restrict travel—how will the adventurers get across the rushing river? Once the appropriate vehicles or tools are discovered, these rivers can actually serve as connective arteries to deeper sections of the Underworld. Boats can be used to travel rivers to hitherto inaccessible sections.

701.title: Example
701.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 19. River › Example
701.body: The River Phlegethon looks like a normal river but the water is acidic, earning it the nickname the “River of Fire.” It exudes a noxious, sulfurous scent. Any normal item submerged into the waters is quickly destroyed. If the guild can persuade Iago the Lion-Turtle to take them onto his back, he can wade and withstand the waters of this river, ferrying them to the other side.

702.title: 20. Waterwheel
702.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 20. Waterwheel
702.body: Waterwheels harness the power of the strange rivers of the Underworld. Adventurers may find the state of the dungeon changed if a waterwheel is stopped or started.

703.title: Example
703.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 20. Waterwheel › Example
703.body: The flow of the river is split into three waterfalls by a series of locks and dams controlled by levers inside the dungeon. When the water turns the northern waterwheel, the colossal door to the Necropolis of Ot is raised. When the water turns the eastern waterwheel, the lamps inside the Castle of Crossed Destinies are lit, allowing adventurers to forgo carrying their own torches. When the water turns the western waterwheel, the bridge extends from the castle towards the City of Ruin. Only one waterfall can flow at a time.

704.title: 21. Well
704.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 21. Well
704.body: Wells in the Underworld contain bizarre things: wine, treacle, oil, pudding. Almost anything but water. Moreover, wells frequently have some denizen who lives off their contents, either dwelling at the bottom of the well or guarding it from interlopers.

705.title: Example
705.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting rooms › 21. Well › Example
705.body: A tiny blue imp lives at the bottom of a wishing well. He demands you throw coins down and he’ll grant you wishes. He is a liar. He wants to make fun of your desires and dreams.

706.title: Creating interesting traps
706.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting traps
706.body: Traps are a genre staple. Here are some principles for creating interesting traps. Traps are usually present to guard something specific . The presence of a trap will tell the players that there is something worthwhile to be gained by braving the trap. Gambling risk and reward is an interesting choice for the players. Create meaningful exploration by telegraphing the presence of traps and having the players figure out how to safely get past them. It’s boring if a trap triggers while an adventurer walks down a hall, deals a Wound, and the adventurer says “OK. I keep going, I guess.” Traps, like the rest of the game, should involve interesting decisions. Telegraph the traps by engaging all five senses. Clues that a trap exists can be found in discolorations of stone, strong smells, grinding gears in walls, temperature differences in the air, etc. If the players follow up on these clues, the traps should be obvious. The essential puzzle is how to overcome the trap, not whether or not a trap exists. As players investigate traps, speak generously and tell them everything their adventurers can see and understand. Traps should be fun for the entire guild. There are no talents that determine who can pick locks or disable devices. Anybody can interact with traps with the right equipment. Arbitrate the players’ actions fairly. Good ideas, preparation, and lateral thinking obviate tests of fate. When players start testing fate, they’ve already failed to deal with the trap in a safe way. Put some of these traps in your dungeon. Use them as inspiration for your own.

707.title: 1. Mysterious tower, acid lake
707.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting traps › 1. Mysterious tower, acid lake
707.body: There is a tumbledown tower in the middle of an island. The island is in the middle of a bright-green acid lake. The lake is death for whoever falls into it. Why this trap doesn’t suck: The possible rewards are tantalizing. (A mysterious tower? What’s in it?) The dangers are obvious. (The lake is bright green! Acid is deadly!) This is an open-ended problem with many possible solutions but no one obvious solution. How to run it: Living creatures who fall into the waters are killed. Unless the player is as direct as saying, “I run and jump in the lake!,” let them test fate to avoid this. Players should be able to easily experiment to determine how caustic the waters actually are. An item will quickly be Destroyed if placed in the acid lake unless it is indestructible. Carefully touching an item to the surface of the acidic water will simply Notch it. Spells might help the guild cross the lake. Gust of Wind would allow one adventurer to cross the lake (more if more Resolve is spent). Defy Depths would probably work, but the adventurer’s boots would burn off their feet as they walked on the surface. Clever guilds might employ the use of flying monsters elsewhere in the dungeon to help them cross the acidic lake.

708.title: 2. Arrow trap
708.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting traps › 2. Arrow trap
708.body: A hallway has a 10’ stretch of wall, dotted with small holes on either side. The floor contains a pressure plate. Stepping on the pressure plate causes arrows to fire from the holes. Why this trap doesn’t suck: Pressure plates and traps (arrows, pits, jets of flame, etc.) are genre staples. That’s cool. However, they tend to be both hidden and deadly. That’s a bad combination during play. You can make these traps not suck by broadcasting the danger clearly and providing a part of the trap for the players to interact with. In this circumstance, the holes are both obvious and interactable. Apply this principle to other types of traps to make tropey traps more fun. How to run it: If an adventurer steps onto the pressure plate, tell the player they hear a click. They have a split second of real-life time to tell you what they want to do. If they make a move away from the holes—dropping to the floor, launching themselves backwards—they can test Pentacles to avoid the volley. On a failure—or if they do nothing—they take a Wound. The arrows will only fire once. (They need to be reset after they’re triggered.) If one adventurer triggers the trap, the rest can pass. The holes on the wall should be a clear indication of danger. Adventurers can trigger the trap prematurely by throwing something heavy onto the pressure plate. They can also leap over it with a successful test of Pentacles. They might plug the holes up with alchemical glue bombs. Let ideas that make sense automatically work.

709.title: 3. Quicksand
709.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting traps › 3. Quicksand
709.body: A swampy section of ground is actually quicksand. It begins to inexorably swallow anybody who steps into it—just like the old movies. Why this trap doesn’t suck: Tropes are instantly understood at the table. Quicksand is a good trope because it’s hidden without being deadly. It traps one adventurer and gives the rest of the guild something to do. How to run it: If the guild is not moving carefully, the first adventurer in the marching order blunders into the quicksand and gets stuck. Unless they have a tool in their hand or on their belt that could help them with the situation (e.g., rope to lasso over a nearby tree limb), they can’t do anything by themselves to get unstuck. Other members of the guild can test Swords to pull the stuck adventurer out: rope grants favor to this test.

710.title: 4. Electrified chest
710.breadcrumb: Appendix E: Underworld Creation › Dungeon Seeds › Creating interesting traps › 4. Electrified chest
